title: CML Lab - Command Center
description: Single-pane view of the spine-leaf lab: node inventory and state history, link status and error rates, compute headroom, and the Pi that scrapes it all.

panels.title: Lab state
panels.description: The lab's own state as CML reports it.

panels.title: Nodes booted
panels.description: Nodes that reached BOOTED, out of 8 in phase 1.

panels.title: Links down
panels.description: Anything above zero is a broken adjacency.

panels.title: CPU oversubscription
panels.description: Cores CML thinks the running nodes need, over the six the box actually has.

panels.title: Drops (1h)
panels.description: Frames the virtual wire lost in the last hour.

panels.title: CML API
panels.description: Whether the exporter could reach the CML API on its last scrape.

panels.title: Node inventory
panels.description: Every node in the lab, with what it is, what state it is in, and what it is consuming right now.

panels.title: Node state history
panels.description: A red band is a node that was not BOOTED. Read it left to right to see exactly when a reload happened.

panels.title: Per-node CPU
panels.description: IOL nodes idle near 1%. A sustained climb is a control-plane loop.

panels.title: Per-node RAM
panels.description: Percent of each node's own allocation, not of the host.

panels.title: Link inventory
panels.description: Every virtual wire, its endpoints, both directions of traffic, and its error rate.

panels.title: Link state history
panels.description: Flapping shows up here as stripes. A steady green bar per link is what a healthy fabric looks like.

panels.title: Per-link throughput
panels.description: Both directions summed, from CML's own link counters.

panels.title: Packet drops per link
panels.description: The error-rate view. Flat on zero is correct; anything else is a starved vSwitch.

panels.title: Compute CPU
panels.description: Actual utilisation. It is the boot storm that hurts, not steady state.

panels.title: Compute memory used
panels.description: 20.5 GB total. Memory has never been the constraint here -- cores are.

panels.title: Nodes running on compute
panels.description: Across every lab on this compute, not just the selected one.

panels.title: CPU demand vs physical capacity
panels.description: Physical cores is a limit, not a series -- grey and dashed, so the two real measures read against it.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Compare against 6 cores: sustained load above 6 is real contention.

panels.title: Raspberry Pi (the box doing the monitoring)
Pi temperature
panels.description: Throttling starts around 80 C. This is the closest thing to a power reading the lab has -- the nodes are virtual, so there is no PSU or PDU to measure.

panels.title: Pi network errors
panels.description: Errors on the Pi's own NIC. Flat zero means the metrics pipeline itself is not the problem.
